title: Binary Search: Interval Conventions and Boundary Updates (Easy Quiz)
evidence_note: The supplied fixture (fixture_binary_search_en) directly supports a single easy-level concept question about the closed-interval [left, right] convention, its initialization, and its loop condition.
learning_objectives: Identify the closed-interval [left, right] convention used by the described exact-match binary search.
State the initial values of left and right and the loop condition for the closed interval.

questions.stem: According to the supplied notes (fixture_binary_search_en), in the closed-interval exact-match binary search on an ascending array of n distinct values, which description correctly states the initial boundaries and the loop condition?
options: left = 0, right = n - 1, and the loop runs while left <= right
left = 0, right = n, and the loop runs while left < right
left = 0, right = n - 1, and the loop runs while left < right
left = 0, right = n, and the loop runs while left <= right
questions.explanation: The notes state that for the closed interval [left, right], left starts at zero and right starts at n minus one, and the loop runs while left <= right; an empty interval means the target is absent.
questions.difficulty_reason: This is an easy item: it asks the student to recognize one explicitly stated convention (initial boundaries and loop condition) directly from the notes, with all conditions given and no strategy selection required.

concepts: initial boundaries left = 0 and right = n - 1
expected_steps: Recall that the closed interval starts with left = 0 and right = n - 1.
Recall that the loop continues while left <= right.

visual_prompt: A horizontal row of array cells labeled 0 to n-1, with a bracket spanning from index 0 to index n-1 labeled '[left, right] closed interval', and a small caption showing 'left = 0, right = n - 1; loop while left <= right'. No answer to any quiz item is shown.
